solutions.text: \(\frac{10}{3}\) Using the Pythagorean theorem, we see that the legs of \(T\) each have length 13. Let \(r\) be the radius of \(\omega_{1}\). We can divide \(T\) into three triangles, each with two vertices at vertices of \(T\) and one vertex at the center of \(\omega_{1}\). These triangles all have height \(r\) and have bases 13,13 , and 10 . Thus their total area is \(\frac{13 r}{2}+\frac{13 r}{2}+\frac{10 r}{2}=18 r\). However, \(T\) has height 12 and base 10 , so its area is 60 . Thus \(18 r=60\), so \(r=\frac{10^{2}}{3}\).
